items.recapEn: Hana woke at four in cold Totsuka and watched the sky turn from black to blue to something between red and white. Downstairs, the innkeeper's daughter Ogawa-san, a student, told her breakfast was seven to eight and the Fujisawa bus took thirty minutes; Hana and Ken would take two hours. At seven, Ken asked the time. Seven, Ken. Seven.

items.recapEn: At the front desk just after six, Hana met Ogawa-san, the innkeeper's daughter, and asked when breakfast was (seven to eight), where the breakfast room was, when to give up the room (ten) and when the Fujisawa bus ran. Ogawa-san studies in Fujisawa and takes the 8:30 bus daily. A forgotten pen was Ken's; Ken was still in bed.

items.recapEn: The handwritten notice in the room at the Totsuka inn, in Ogawa-san's hand: breakfast seven to eight behind the white door, bath six to eleven beyond the black door, rooms until ten, keys on the desk downstairs, the Fujisawa bus times, and who is on the desk: Ogawa-san in the morning, her parents the rest of the day.
